cells.tense: You are sitting with someone's experience without needing it to become yours.
cells.ask: Tell one person you work with that you can tell something is going on for them. Leave out the part where you fix it.
cells.core:
There's a difference between caring about someone and feeling alongside them, and you're doing the second. When a person near you has some weight on them, you don't take the weight over and you don't stand back from it either. You stay yourself and you stay close, which is harder than either one alone.

The next piece is to hold that under someone else's pressure. When they lean on you more than feels comfortable, the move is to stay where you are instead of absorbing it. That's not coldness. It's how the closeness lasts, and it's what lets the other person keep their own ground too.
cells.sheetLine: You stay close without disappearing into someone else.
cells.verb: feeling with someone rather than about them
cells.place: in the space between you and another person

cells.tense: You will be flooded by whatever the next person around you is carrying.
cells.ask: When someone tells you what's wrong today, wait three seconds before you respond. Then say it back with their name in the sentence.
cells.core:
You can feel with people, and this is running ahead of you. The mood of whoever's nearby arrives before they've said anything — you're anticipating it, shaping yourself around it, living out the hard thing you're not responsible for. By the time they speak, you've already been through it.

When this is working, one person's day stays that person's day and yours stays yours. You can tell which is which by staying in yourself for a breath before you answer. Everything you're bracing against isn't yours to carry, and the not-carrying is the thing you can practise today. That is the separation the feeling needs, and it is what keeps the closeness from swallowing you whole.
cells.sheetLine: You're already feeling what the next person might need.
cells.verb: feeling with someone rather than about them
cells.place: in the space between you and another person

cells.tense: You stopped arriving in the room with others a long time ago.
cells.ask: In one conversation today, ask a follow-up question about something the person mentioned. Then sit through the answer without changing the subject.
cells.core:
The connection hasn't vanished but it's running shallow. You talk to people, you get along, and you stay near the surface. Questions get asked and answers get given and nothing of yours is in the exchange, so nothing of theirs lands either. It's not that you don't care. The habit of leaning toward someone else has gone quiet.

When this is working, you're still in the room after the small talk ends. You notice the thing sitting behind what someone said, and you go one step closer instead of away. The repair isn't to feel more. Stay one beat longer than you usually do, on something small, and let the next sentence happen without you steering it.
cells.sheetLine: You're there. You just aren't in the conversation.
cells.verb: feeling with someone rather than about them
cells.place: in the space between you and another person

cells.tense: You are already moved by other people, though you call it just paying attention.
cells.ask: Say out loud, to one person, something you did this week because you cared about how they were doing. Call it caring.
cells.core:
The feeling is running — people notice it, they soften around it — but you've filed it under practical and moved on. You show up when something matters. You remember a hard date, you make room, you ask the question nobody else asks. Someone on the other end feels that as care, and they are not wrong.

When this is working, you'd say so plainly instead of letting them guess. That thing you did, the one they never asked about, you say it was done because you wanted them to be all right. That sentence doesn't need a speech about who you are. It's just true, once, out loud, to one person who already felt it. The name for what you're doing is yours to claim.
cells.sheetLine: The care is there. You just won't call it by its name.
